thread:
Maya: Heads-up — after the metering-api v2 rollout this morning we're seeing a persistent ~1-3% delta between ingestion events and invoice line items for long-running chat sessions. sample: `session_duration > 30m` seems most affected. Anyone else seeing this?
Raj: Yea noticed it. v2 changed the fingerprinting key from `session_id` -> `client_session_key`; router obfuscation strips `client_id` in some paths so we lose the canonical id for aggregation. some events land as separate short sessions instead of one long session.
Olivia: Is this the change we planned for privacy-preserving session keys? we flagged that for docs but didn't push console UX notes. customers will see weird billing gaps.
Dave: Telemetry shows a spike in late-arrival events too (ingest timestamp vs event timestamp skew). Also our dedupe depends on `event_id` which v2 omitted for a subset of proxied requests.
Maya: Example log lines from the ingest pipeline:
```
WARN 2026-05-03T10:12:04Z ingest: dropped field event_id=null path=/v2/metering payload="{...}"
INFO 2026-05-03T10:12:18Z normalize: fallback fingerprint used: (client_id,evt_ts) for tenant=acme-inc
```
Raj: Quick fix idea: re-enable fallback fingerprinting to `(client_id, event_ts)` in the router for 12-24h until we can backfill and reconcile. longer term we should add a canonical `session_fingerprint` signed by edge that isn't stripped.
Olivia: UX side — we should expose `ingestion_version` per-route in the Console and a \"billing confidence\" badge on the invoice preview so customers aren't surprised during rollouts. feature-flag that so we can flip on for internal accounts first.
Dave: Operational proposal: canary v2 at 5% of tenants + telemetry checks: if invoice-delta > 0.5% sustained for 4h, auto-alert #incidents and pause rollout. Also run a backfill job for 48h window for customers routed to v2.
metering-bot: deploy metering-api v2 finished deploy: metering-api:v2.3.1 -> prod (canary=5%).
Maya: For reconciliation, here's a quick sampling query to compare ingested tokens vs billed tokens for a tenant: 
```
SELECT tenant_id, SUM(ingested_tokens) as ingest_tokens, SUM(billed_tokens) as billed_tokens, (SUM(ingested_tokens)-SUM(billed_tokens)) as delta
FROM token_events
WHERE tenant_id = 'acme-inc' AND event_ts >= now() - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY tenant_id;
```
Raj: Agree on fallback + backfill. Prefer patch over rollback. Steps: 1) toggle router fallback flag (immediate), 2) launch backfill job for last 72 hours, 3) add strict schema validation in v2 with soft-errors (log + metric) for missing event_id/session_fingerprint, 4) add signed `session_fingerprint` header on edge.
Olivia: I'll add the Console tickets: (a) ingestion_version badge, (b) billing confidence metric & tooltip, (c) rollout view for metering API so customers can see which version they're on.
Dave: I'll wire an automated dashboard and anomaly alert: compare 7d rolling ingest vs billed ratio per-tenant; threshold 0.5% as Raj suggested. Also instrument latency buckets for late-arrival events and mark them in the reconciliation UI.
Maya: Can we also publish a quick customer note? short post in status.redwood.ai and a banner in Console for affected tenants while we reconcile.
Raj: I'll own the fallback toggle and backfill job. Dave — can you share the dashboard link when ready?
Dave: will do, ping me here when backfill starts.
Olivia: tagging product-ops: we need comms copy.
Maya: thanks everyone. tagging @metering-bot for the roll-forward checklist and we can close once delta < 0.2% for 48h. :thumbsup:
Raj: ack.
Dave: ack :rocket:
